theme: The 〜ば conditional — "if..." for advice and general rules
intro: Meet 〜ば, the cousin of 〜たら — great for general truths, hypotheticals, and "what should I do?" phrases when asking a local for tips.

grammar.title: The 〜ば conditional

rules.label: る-verbs
examples: 食べる → 食べれば (if one eats)

rules.label: う-verbs
rules.detail: change final -u to -e, then add ば
examples: 行く → 行けば (if one goes)
飲む → 飲めば (if one drinks)
話す → 話せば (if one speaks)

rules.label: い-adjectives
rules.detail: drop い, add ければ
examples: 安い → 安ければ (if cheap)
いい → よければ (if good)

rules.label: な-adj / nouns
examples: 静か → 静かなら (if quiet)

rules.label: Negative
examples: 行かない → 行かなければ (if one doesn't go)

grammar.bigPoint: When the main clause is a request or command ("if..., please do X"), Japanese usually prefers 〜たら over 〜ば. Advice/general result → 〜ば; "if it happens, please do X" → 〜たら.

vocab.jp: 乗り換える（のりかえる）

examples.en: If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

examples.jp: この道をまっすぐ行けば、駅があります。
examples.romaji: Kono michi o massugu ikeba, eki ga arimasu.
examples.en: If you go straight down this road, you'll find the station.

examples.jp: どうすれば、電車を予約できますか。
examples.romaji: Dō sureba, densha o yoyaku dekimasu ka.
examples.en: How can I book the train?

note: 〜ば spotlights the condition itself, so it's the go-to for general "if X, then naturally Y" statements and advice. A handy set phrase is 〜ばいい = "you should / it'd be good to 〜": 早く予約すればいいですよ (Hayaku yoyaku sureba ii desu yo) = "You should book early."

selfCheck.q: Fill the blank: 「＿＿、電話してください。」 (困る/こまる = to be in trouble) — "If you're in trouble, please call." The main clause is a request — which conditional fits best?
selfCheck.a: 〜たら: 「困ったら、電話してください」 (Komattara, denwa shite kudasai). Because the main clause is a request, 〜たら is natural; 困れば would sound odd here. Rule: advice/general result → 〜ば; "if it happens, please do X" → 〜たら.
